text:
maria: heads up — started seeing a ~20% p95/p99 tail latency regression on H100 FP8 workloads after last night's runtime roll. L40S jobs for the same model/config look stable. anyone else seeing this? :thinking:

devin: which run id / model? can you paste a small perf snapshot and the kernel flags used?

maria: run_id r-20260318-13. model redwood/llama-7b-fp8. kernel flags: transformer_engine_fp8=true, kernel=fp8_tile32. quick perf dump:
```
run_id: r-20260318-13
hw: H100
model: redwood/llama-7b-fp8
config: transformer_engine_fp8=true; kernel=fp8_tile32; batcher=adaptive
p50: 45ms (unchanged)
p95: 210ms (was 170ms)
p99: 420ms (was 300ms)
kv_hit_rate: 0.82
batch_size_distribution: {1:70%, 2:20%, >=4:10%}
```

li: rough guess — this smells like a kernel slowpath under microbatch (batch=1) + long sequence mixing. any kv-miss/eviction noise? can you paste profiler summary?

maria: profiler snippet attached (trimmed):
```
profiling_summary:
  total_tokens: 4.1M
  kernel_switch_count: 34
  fallback_int8_count: 3
  kv_evictions: 6
  cuda_stream_wait_us: [avg: 120, p95: 480]
  launch_overhead_ms: up 12% vs baseline
```

anika: if L40S is fine, could be TE (Transformer Engine) kernel on H100 choosing a different micro-tile size for fp8. H100's fast paths sometimes regress when seq_len distribution shifts. did the rollout change any TE config?

maria: rollout only flipped a quantization calibration change (we moved from per-tensor to per-channel pilot for fp8). that change landed late yesterday.

devin: try toggling calibration mode back to per-tensor as a quick A/B. env flags: TE_FP8_CALIB=per_tensor or per_channel. also try TE_FP8_EPS tweak (e.g., 1e-7 vs 1e-6). can you run microbench with --seq-len 512/1024 and batch=1/4 to reproduce?

maria: ran a small microbench. results:
```
H100 FP8 (per_channel): seq=512 batch=1 p95=230ms p99=460ms
H100 FP8 (per_tensor): seq=512 batch=1 p95=180ms p99=320ms
H100 int8_fallback: seq=512 batch=1 p95=175ms p99=310ms
L40S FP8 (per_channel): seq=512 batch=1 p95=175ms p99=305ms
```
so per-channel calibration looks slower on H100 specifically. int8 fallback is comparable to per-tensor fp8.

li: interesting — points at kernel selection differences on H100 when per-channel quantized layout changes math kernel (maybe smaller tile or extra kernel wrappers). can you capture kernel names from the profiler (cupti/kern logs)?

maria: pasted kernel list (top hot kernels):
```
fp8_tile32_dot (calls: 1.2M)
fp8_tile64_dot (calls: 0.3M)
int8_slow_dot (calls: 0.05M)
fp8_reduce_cast (calls: 0.02M)
```
but on H100 per-channel runs we see more `fp8_reduce_cast` and `fp8_tile64_dot` entries (those have higher launch overhead on our stack).

devin: ok actionable plan:
- short-term: add a routing heuristic to prefer int8 path for (seq_len>512 && batch==1) on H100 until TE patch lands
- medium: instrument kernel selector to log "selected_kernel" metric for every request; aggregate by seq_len/batch/kalman-state
- long-term: work with TE upstream on kernel tile heuristics for per-channel fp8 on H100.

maria: canaryed a kernel_policy change to route problem cases to int8 — quick results show p99 dropping back to ~320ms on canary (matches per_tensor fp8).

li: we need to check quality impact of int8 fallback on common prompts. can you run eval on the standard prompt-set with 200 samples?

maria: ran eval, delta in token-level perplexity ~+0.4% and no visible generation regressions on our perf eval prompts. small quality hit but probably acceptable as mitigation.

anika: added infra test job to run nightly microbench matrix across H100/L40S with per-channel/per-tensor flags so we catch regressions earlier.

ops-bot: deploy: canary updated — kernel_policy v1.2 applied to 8% of traffic (by region) at 2026-03-18T21:04Z.

devin: I'll push a small selector-logging change to prod branch (emit metrics: selected_kernel, seq_len, batch_size, kv_hit) — should help root cause. leaving a TODO for TE upstream. :thumbsup:

maria: thanks team — leaving canary for 6h and will report if anything odd reappears. if we see impact on cost/Q we can revert.

li: one more note — we should add a unit that simulates per-channel quant layout in our local perf harness so kernel differences show up in CI. filing issue.

maria: filed #INFRA-1421 with repro steps and the microbench commands. closing for now unless we see more anomalies.
